The technical specification has been translated into an unabridged, end-to-end prompt optimized for zero-overhead inference on serverless infrastructure. The prompt specifies the deployment of the 262,144-token context multimodal hybrid MoE architecture using non-standard acceleration techniques.

***

## Deployment Prompt

```text
Construct a complete, production-ready, serverless multimodal inference engine deployed on Modal (modal.com). The system must serve a hybrid linear-attention/full-attention Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) vision-language foundation model supporting a full 262,144-token context window, maximal output token generation, and concurrent high-resolution image/video inputs. 

Do not use high-latency initialization loops, unquantized baseline forward passes, or runtime weight transfers. Implement custom high-throughput CUDA/Triton kernels for block-wise FP8 computation, hybrid memory-mapped weight streaming from Modal Volumes with flash-boot snapshots, and an interleaved speculative decoding verifier.

Deliver all source files in full, unabridged code without placeholders, stubs, ellipses, or simulated routines.

### System Architecture and Model Specifications

1. Core Text Backbone Configuration:
   - Context window: 262,144 tokens (`max_position_embeddings: 262144`).
   - Vocabulary size: 248,320 tokens (`vocab_size: 248320`, `bos_token_id: 248044`, `eos_token_id: 248044`).
   - Dimensions: Hidden size 2,560, 48 hidden layers (`num_hidden_layers: 48`).
   - Layer Pattern: Interleaved repeating structure where every 4th layer is Full Attention (`full_attention_interval: 4`), and all other 3 intervening layers are Linear Attention (State-Space / Linear Conv).
   - Linear Attention Specifications: Convolution kernel dimension 4 (`linear_conv_kernel_dim: 4`), key head dimension 128 (`linear_key_head_dim: 128`), value head dimension 128 (`linear_value_head_dim: 128`), 16 key heads (`linear_num_key_heads: 16`), and 48 value heads (`linear_num_value_heads: 48`).
   - Full Attention Specifications: 24 attention heads (`num_attention_heads: 24`, `head_dim: 256`), 2 key-value heads (`num_key_value_heads: 2`), sparse indexer routing budget 2,048 (`indexer_budget: 2048`, `indexer_compress_ratio: 4`, `indexer_head_dim: 128`, `indexer_n_heads: 4`, `indexer_kv_heads: 1`).
   - Rotary Embeddings: Multimodal Interleaved RoPE (mRoPE) partitioned across 3 sections [11, 11, 10] (`mrope_section: [11, 11, 10]`), partial rotary factor 0.25 (`partial_rotary_factor: 0.25`), base theta 10,000,000.0 (`rope_theta: 10000000.0`).
   - HyperConnection Mixer: Residual stream hyperconnections with rank-320 bottleneck (`hc_count: 4`, `hc_lowrank: 320`) per attention and MLP block with `input_mix_weight_down`, `input_mix_weight_up`, and `block_inject_weight`.
   - Prior Layer Enhancement (PLE): Conv1D kernel size 4 and embedding dimension 2,560 on designated layers (`ple_layer_ids: [2]`).
   - Mixture of Experts (MoE): 512 total routed experts (`num_experts: 512`), 10 active experts per token (`num_experts_per_tok: 10`), routed intermediate size 640 (`moe_intermediate_size: 640`), plus 1 dedicated shared expert (`shared_expert_intermediate_size: 640`) with sigmoid gating.
   - Multi-Token Prediction (MTP): 1-layer hybrid speculative draft module with projection matrices (`mtp_num_hidden_layers: 1`, `ngram_size: 3`) verifying speculative n-grams in parallel.

2. Multimodal Vision Encoder Configuration:
   - Vision Transformer: 27 depth layers (`depth: 27`), hidden dimension 1,152 (`hidden_size: 1152`), 16 attention heads (`num_heads: 16`), MLP intermediate dimension 4,304 (`intermediate_size: 4304`), `gelu_pytorch_tanh` activation.
   - Spatial/Temporal Merging: Patch size 16x16 (`patch_size: 16`), temporal patch size 2 (`temporal_patch_size: 2`), 2D spatial merge size 2x2 (`spatial_mergesize: 2`), projected to text hidden dimension 2,560 (`out_hidden_size: 2560`).
   - Special Token Delimiters: `vision_start_token_id: 248053`, `vision_end_token_id: 248054`, `image_token_id: 248056`, `video_token_id: 248057`.

3. Quantization and Memory Layout:
   - Quantization Format: Block-wise FP8 (`quant_method: fp8`, `weight_block_size: [128, 128]`, dynamic activation scaling).
   - Precision Exceptions: Normalization layers, embeddings (`embed_tokens`), hyperconnection mixers, PLE convolutions, and linear attention 1D convolutions remain in float32 / bfloat16.

### Infrastructure, Cold-Start, and GPU Strategy

1. GPU Allocation and Cost Efficiency:
   - Target Hardware: Deploy on a multi-GPU configuration (such as 2x or 4x NVIDIA L40S 48GB or NVIDIA A100/H100 NVLink) optimized to maintain the entire 512-expert FP8 parameter set and dynamic KV-cache across 262,144 positions without out-of-memory errors while minimizing hourly execution cost.
   - Cold-Start Elimination: Persist weights in a high-speed Modal Volume with sequential chunk indexing. Pre-compile Triton kernels during image build (`modal.Image.dockerfile_commands` / `run_function`). Utilize Modal snapshotting and memory-mapped direct CUDA allocation (`torch.UntypedStorage.from_file`) to bypass CPU-to-GPU transfer bottlenecks.

2. Serving Engine Architecture:
   - Paged Attention and State-Space Ring Buffer: Paged KV-cache manager for Full Attention layers and fixed-size circular state buffers for Linear Attention layers.
   - Continuous Batching and Scheduling: Radix-tree prefix cache reuse for shared prompt prefixes and vision token sequences.
   - Async Web Server: FastAPI server providing OpenAI-compatible endpoints (`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/models`) supporting Server-Sent Events (SSE) token streaming, multi-image base64 decoding, and video frame tensor batching.

### Required Source Files and Implementation Deliverables

Implement the complete codebase across the following structured files:

- `engine/config.py`: Complete dataclass configurations matching the exact parameters for text backbone, vision encoder, MoE routing, MTP speculative head, and FP8 block quantization.
- `engine/kernels.py`: Custom Triton kernels for block-wise FP8 matrix multiplication (`[128, 128]` tile scaling), mRoPE interleaved position application, and fused linear-attention causal 1D conv + state-space step.
- `engine/vision.py`: Vision Transformer implementation supporting dynamic image resolution grid partitioning, 3D video temporal-patch extraction, 2D merge projection, and multimodal token interleaving.
- `engine/model.py`: Neural network implementation containing HyperConnection mixers, PLE blocks, 512-expert Top-10 MoE sparse router with shared expert fusion, 48-layer hybrid attention backbone, and MTP speculative decoding head.
- `engine/kv_cache.py`: Hybrid Paged KV-cache manager supporting 256k-token contexts, dynamic page allocation, and Linear Attention recurrent state buffers.
- `engine/sampler.py`: Speculative MTP tree-verification sampler and continuous batching scheduler.
- `app.py`: Modal application script defining `modal.App`, custom container image dependencies, Volume mounts, memory-mapped prewarming, container lifecycle methods (`@app.cls`), and streaming FastAPI endpoints.
- `client.py`: End-to-end client script demonstrating multimodal inference requests containing text, ultra-high-resolution images, and video clips up to full context limits.

Ensure all tensor operations adhere strictly to PyTorch and Triton standards with correct dimension broadcasting, tensor parallelism hooks, dynamic FP8 scaling math, and strict input validation.
```

***

## Optimization Strategy

The architecture avoids standard bottlenecks through targeted kernel fusion, zero-copy weight hydration, and hybrid cache management.

| Design Component | Standard Approach | High-Performance Serverless Approach |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Weight Loading** | Network HuggingFace pull during startup | Memory-mapped Modal Volume with snapshot caching |
| **MoE Computation** | Unquantized sequential expert dispatch | Block-wise FP8 GEMM with fused Top-10 routing |
| **Context Management** | Quadratic quadratic attention across 256k tokens | Paged KV-cache paired with recurrent state-space buffers |
| **Multi-Token Output** | Autoregressive single-token decoding | Interleaved Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) tree verification |
| **Hardware Selection** | Over-provisioned unquantized 8x H100 | Cost-effective FP8 multi-L40S / A100 tensor partitioning |

Your previous prompt is directionally strong but has several weaknesses: it does not fully exploit the provided configuration file, it is vague about the exact GPU layout and cost/performance tradeoffs on Modal, and it under-specifies some critical low-level constraints for achieving very low cold start on a cheap-but-fast GPU configuration.[1][2][3][4]

## Main weaknesses

The first weakness is incomplete use of the configuration file. The configuration includes a detailed `quantization_config` with a long `modules_to_not_convert` list, explicit `vision_config`, and a nested `mtp` block, but the prompt only partially reflected these and did not clearly state that all of them must be implemented exactly as specified, without omission. This is a gap because the user explicitly required reading every character and reproducing the full production configuration, including all exceptions and non-quantized modules, not just the high-level hyperparameters.[1]

The second weakness is that the GPU strategy on Modal was left somewhat generic. The prompt mentioned “multi-GPU configuration (such as 2x or 4x L40S or A100/H100)” without committing to a concrete default configuration optimized for “lehető legolcsóbb de leggyorsabb és legrövidebb cold start” (as cheap as possible but fast with minimal cold start), even though Modal’s pricing and GPU catalog make L40S and A10 particularly clear candidates for inference, with L40S at about 0.000542 USD/sec (~1.95 USD/hour) and A10 at 0.000306 USD/sec (~1.10 USD/hour). It also did not clearly separate a default single-GPU L40S deployment (for minimal cost and complexity) from optional multi-GPU scaling patterns.[2][3][4]

The third weakness is that the “cannot use the obvious solution” constraint was not made explicit enough in operational terms. While the architecture is non-obvious (FP8, custom Triton kernels, hybrid attention), the prompt did not forbid relying on generic serving stacks (e.g., generic HF pipelines, vLLM, TGI, or prebuilt Modal examples), nor did it explicitly require building a custom inference runtime and caching subsystem from scratch. This leaves room for an “obvious” implementation path the user explicitly wanted to avoid.[1]

The fourth weakness is that the Modal integration specifics were under-specified. The prompt did not explicitly require the use of Modal’s `gpu` argument with well-defined values (e.g., `"L40S"` or `"A10"`), did not specify concurrency limits, and did not spell out how to combine persistent volumes, pre-baked images, and snapshotting to minimize cold start. It also did not describe a clear plan to pre-compile Triton kernels at image build time and to memory-map weights directly into GPU memory using Modal’s lifecycle hooks.[5][3][4]

The fifth weakness is that the maximum output and full-context constraints were only described qualitatively. The prompt stated that the model supports 262,144-token context and “maximal output token generation” but did not specify concrete behaviors such as enforcing the upper bound in server parameters, streaming tokens until the context limit is reached, and configuring pagination of KV cache to keep 262k context without blowing GPU memory.[1]

Below is a tightened, stronger prompt that addresses these issues.

## Revised deployment prompt

The following prompt explicitly reuses and restates the configuration from the provided `config.json` file, requiring exact implementation of all parameters and quantization exceptions. It also fixes the GPU strategy for Modal (default single L40S with optional scale-out), makes the “no obvious solution” constraint operational, and strengthens the requirements for low cold start and full-context, multimodal, max-output behavior.[3][4][2][1]

```text
Construct a complete, production-grade multimodal inference system deployed on Modal, implementing the exact model, vision, MTP, and quantization configuration described in the provided configuration file, without omitting any parameter or module.[file:1]

Implement a hybrid text–vision–video Mixture-of-Experts model with a 262,144-token context window and maximum-length output generation, running on a serverless Modal deployment that scales to zero and restarts with minimal cold start while remaining as inexpensive as possible under the constraint that it must still be fast and high-throughput.[file:1][web:12]

Do not use any generic or prebuilt serving stack such as generic HuggingFace pipelines, vLLM, TGI, or any Modal example projects. Implement a custom inference engine from scratch, including model definition, attention kernels, KV/state management, batching, scheduling, and HTTP/WS streaming endpoints. Do not rely on any “obvious solution” involving off-the-shelf high-level serving frameworks or naive full attention over 262k tokens; instead use the specified hybrid attention and quantization design.[file:1]

### Exact model configuration

Implement the text backbone exactly as described by `text_config` in the provided configuration file, including all hyperparameters, layer types, and mixture-of-experts settings:[file:1]

1. Core text architecture:
   - Model type: `qwen4_exp_text` with `hidden_size` 2560, `num_hidden_layers` 48, `num_attention_heads` 24, and `head_dim` 256.[file:1]
   - Context window: `max_position_embeddings` 262144.[file:1]
   - Vocabulary and tokens: `vocab_size` 248320, `bos_token_id` 248044, `eos_token_id` 248044, `pad_token_id` null, `language_model_only` false.[file:1]
   - Activation and normalization: `hidden_act` `"silu"`, `rms_norm_eps` 1e-06, `initializer_range` 0.02.[file:1]
   - Caching: `use_cache` true.[file:1]

2. Layer types and hybrid attention:
   - Implement the exact `layer_types` array: a repeating pattern of `"linear_attention"` and `"full_attention"` such that every 4th layer is full attention, with all other layers using the linear-attention variant.[file:1]
   - For linear attention layers, implement the specified parameters: `linear_conv_kernel_dim` 4, `linear_key_head_dim` 128, `linear_value_head_dim` 128, `linear_num_key_heads` 16, `linear_num_value_heads` 48, and `mamba_ssm_dtype` `"float32"`.[file:1]
   - For full attention layers, implement key–value heads and indexer configuration: `num_key_value_heads` 2, `indexer_budget` 2048, `indexer_compress_ratio` 4, `indexer_head_dim` 128, `indexer_n_heads` 4, `indexer_kv_heads` 1, and `heads_per_ngram` 8.[file:1]

3. Rotary and mRoPE:
   - Implement rope parameters as specified in `rope_parameters`: `mrope_interleaved` true, `mrope_section` [11, 11, 10], `partial_rotary_factor` 0.25, `rope_theta` 10000000, `rope_type` `"default"`.[file:1]
   - Apply these parameters consistently across both base text layers and the MTP head so that position encodings remain aligned.[file:1]

4. HyperConnection and PLE:
   - Implement HyperConnection mixers with `hc_count` 4 and `hc_lowrank` 320 for both attention and MLP blocks, using the exact structure implied by the module names in `modules_to_not_convert` for `hyper_connection_mixer.input_mix_weight_down`, `input_mix_weight_up`, and `block_inject_weight`.[file:1]
   - Implement Prior Layer Enhancement (PLE) according to `ple_conv_kernel_size` 4, `ple_embed_dim` 2560, and `ple_layer_ids` [2], including both the convolution and projection components referenced by `ple.conv1d`, `key_proj`, and `value_proj` module names.[file:1]

5. Mixture of Experts and shared expert:
   - Implement a 512-expert routed MoE with `num_experts` 512 and `num_experts_per_tok` 10, `moe_intermediate_size` 640, and `shared_expert_intermediate_size` 640.[file:1]
   - Implement gating with `output_gate_type` `"sigmoid"`, `router_aux_loss_coef` 0.001, and `output_router_logits` false.[file:1]
   - Implement shared expert modules and gates exactly as implied by `mlp.shared_expert.*` and `mlp.shared_expert_gate` paths, including all per-layer hyperconnections.[file:1]

6. Multi-token prediction (MTP):
   - Implement the MTP block as specified: `mtp` object with `hybrid` true, `layer_types` ["full_attention"], `num_hidden_layers` 1, `rope_theta` 10000000, and `mtp_num_hidden_layers` 1.[file:1]
   - Configure MTP vocabulary and n-grams: `ngram_size` 3, `ngram_vocab_size_base` 20000000, `make_ngram_vocab_size_divisible_by` 128, and `split_ngram_parts` 128, with `mtp_use_dedicated_embeddings` false and `mtp_use_hidden_state_from_layer` null.[file:1]
   - Implement associated MTP modules (`mtp.fc_embedding`, `mtp.fc_hidden`, `mtp.layers.0.*`) as separate FP8-quantized layers with preserved non-quantized modules exactly matching the config.[file:1]

### Vision and multimodal configuration

Implement the vision model and multimodal integration exactly as specified in `vision_config` and the top-level multimodal settings:[file:1]

1. Vision encoder:
   - `model_type`: `"qwen4_exp"` for the vision config block, `hidden_size` 1152, `depth` 27, `num_heads` 16, `intermediate_size` 4304, `hidden_act` `"gelu_pytorch_tanh"`, `in_channels` 3.[file:1]
   - Patching and merging: `patch_size` 16, `spatial_merge_size` 2, `temporal_patch_size` 2, `num_position_embeddings` 2304, `out_hidden_size` 2560.[file:1]
   - Implement all visual blocks and merger layers implied by the module paths: `model.visual.blocks.*.attn.qkv`, `attn.proj`, `mlp.linear_fc1`, `mlp.linear_fc2`, `model.visual.merger.linear_fc1`, `linear_fc2`, `model.visual.patch_embed.proj`, and `model.visual.pos_embed`.[file:1]

2. Multimodal tokens:
   - Implement `vision_start_token_id` 248053, `vision_end_token_id` 248054, `image_token_id` 248056, `video_token_id` 248057, ensuring the tokenizer and server accept image and video inputs and interleave them with text tokens using these delimiters.[file:1]

3. Multimodal inference behavior:
   - Support high-resolution images (multi-megapixel) by dynamically partitioning them into patches according to `patch_size` and `spatial_merge_size`.
   - Support video clips by slicing into temporal patches using `temporal_patch_size`, batching frames into sequences, and mapping them through the vision stack before projection to `out_hidden_size` and concatenation into the text token stream.

### Quantization and FP8 configuration

Implement FP8 quantization exactly as specified in `quantization_config`:[file:1]

1. Global quantization settings:
   - `quant_method`: `"fp8"`, `activation_scheme`: `"dynamic"`, `weight_per_tensor`: false, `act_per_tensor`: false, `weight_block_size`: [128, 128].[file:1]
   - Implement block-wise FP8 with tile size 128x128 using custom CUDA/Triton kernels, enforcing dynamic scaling for activations and weights.

2. Non-quantized modules:
   - Honor the entire `modules_to_not_convert` list from `quantization_config`, ensuring that every single module name listed remains in higher precision (e.g., float32 or bfloat16), and that no module outside this list is exempted.[file:1]
   - This includes, but is not limited to, `lm_head`, `model.language_model.embed_tokens`, all hyperconnection mixers, PLE modules, linear attention convs and projections, shared experts, MTP layers, and vision attention and MLP layers exactly as enumerated in the configuration.[file:1]
   - Implement a deterministic mapping between module names and quantization behavior, verifying at initialization that the current model’s module tree matches the expected names; fail fast if there is any mismatch.

### GPU strategy and Modal deployment

Optimize for “as cheap as possible but fast and with minimal cold start” on Modal, using a default deployment on a single NVIDIA L40S with optional multi-GPU scale-out.[web:5][web:12][web:13]

1. Default GPU configuration:
   - Use `gpu="L40S"` in Modal functions as the default hardware, leveraging its 48 GB VRAM and inference-optimized profile at approximately 0.000542 USD/sec (~1.95 USD/hour).[web:5][web:12][web:14]
   - Configure the container with minimal CPU cores and memory consistent with GPU utilization (e.g., 1–2 physical cores and 8–16 GiB RAM), taking into account Modal’s per-second CPU and memory rates.[web:12]

2. Optional scale-out:
   - Provide configuration options to run on multiple L40S GPUs per container via `gpu="L40S:n"` for n up to 8, and to switch to A100 or H100/B200 variants (`"A100-40GB"`, `"A100-80GB"`, `"H100"`, `"B200"`) for extremely high-throughput deployments when cost budgets allow.[web:13]
   - Implement tensor or pipeline parallelism across multiple GPUs using NCCL, keeping MTP and MoE routing consistent.

3. Cold start minimization:
   - Store model weights (FP8 quantized) in a Modal Volume and load them via memory-mapped files with `torch.UntypedStorage.from_file` or equivalent, mapping directly into GPU memory where possible to avoid large CPU→GPU transfers.[web:12][web:13]
   - Pre-compile all Triton kernels during image build (Dockerfile / `modal.Image`), so they are ready at container startup, not compiled on first request.
   - Use Modal’s application lifecycle hooks (`@app.cls`, `__enter__`, `__exit__`) to perform one-time warmup: allocate KV-cache pages and linear-attention state buffers, open and map weight files, and run a single dummy forward pass on a short sequence to populate JIT caches.
   - Ensure containers are configured for scale-to-zero with a short idle timeout, but can cold-start to first token in a few hundred milliseconds under realistic conditions.

### Inference engine and server behavior

Implement a custom serving engine tailored to this architecture and Modal:

1. KV cache and state buffer management:
   - Implement a paged KV cache for full attention layers, with fixed-size pages and a mapping from token indices to pages, so that the full 262,144-token context can be served without exhausting GPU memory.[file:1]
   - Implement ring buffers for linear attention state, storing recurrent state per layer and per sequence in a fixed-size buffer, reused and advanced as tokens are appended.
   - Implement efficient eviction and reuse policies to support multiple concurrent requests while respecting the maximum context limit per request.

2. Speculative decoding and MTP:
   - Implement multi-token speculative decoding using the configured MTP head, with n-gram size 3 and hybrid full attention in the MTP layer, verifying drafts against the main model and rolling back when predictions diverge.[file:1]
   - Integrate this with continuous batching: while one request is being verified, other requests can be batched into the same main-model forward pass.

3. Scheduler and batching:
   - Implement a continuous batching scheduler that groups requests by similar prompt lengths and shared prefixes; reuse KV-cache pages when prompts share prefixes.
   - Implement an OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint exposing temperature, top_p, max_tokens, and stop sequences, streaming tokens as Server-Sent Events (SSE) until either stop conditions or the 262,144-token context limit is reached.

4. Multimodal API:
   - Accept image and video inputs as base64-encoded payloads in the request body; decode them into tensors on the server, run them through the vision stack, and interleave their representations with text tokens using the specified multimodal tokens.
   - Implement server-side validation for image/video size and length to keep per-request GPU memory within budget; reject or downsample inputs exceeding safe limits.

- `engine/config.py`: Exact dataclasses mirroring all fields of `text_config`, `vision_config`, `mtp`, and `quantization_config`, including full support for `modules_to_not_convert` and all rope and MoE parameters.[file:1]
- `engine/kernels.py`: Triton/CUDA kernels implementing block-wise FP8 GEMM with tile size [128, 128], fused linear attention (conv1d + state update), and rotary/mRoPE application, pre-compiled at image build.
- `engine/vision.py`: Full vision encoder with patch embedding, positional embeddings, 27 Transformer blocks, MLPs, and merger layers matching the config.[file:1]
- `engine/model.py`: Complete base model including all layers, MoE routers, shared expert, hyperconnections, PLE, and MTP head, with correct routing and FP8 quantization hooks.
- `engine/kv_cache.py`: Paged KV cache and linear state management for 262k context, including multi-request handling.
- `engine/sampler.py`: Sampling logic integrating MTP speculative decoding and streaming output.
- `app.py`: Modal application definition (`modal.App`), custom image and volume configuration, GPU configuration, and FastAPI/ASGI app exposing OpenAI-compatible endpoints on Modal.[web:11][web:13]
- `client.py`: Example client that sends long-context text, high-resolution images, and video clips and reads streaming responses, with parameters set to generate up to the maximum allowable output tokens under the 262,144-token context.

All files must be complete and self-contained. No function, class, or module may be left as a stub, placeholder, or simplified stand-in. All configuration values and module names from the provided configuration file must be honored exactly, and all Modal deployment parameters must be wired so that the system runs on L40S by default with optional scale-out to other GPUs, maximizing performance per dollar while keeping cold start minimal.[file:1][web:5][web:12][web:13]
```
